lesson_title: Your Desk Is Trying to Tell You Something
hook_text: Why does your desk top slope? Why is the seat welded on? Every answer is a designer's decision, and you can read them all.
clip_script: Look at the desk you are sitting at. Steel tubes: light, strong, cheap to weld. The top slopes a little: easier to write on. It is shiny laminate: wipes clean, laughs at ink. A shelf: keeps the top clear. The seat is welded to the frame: nothing gets stolen in pieces and it stands firm. Plastic feet: quiet on the floor. No sharp corners: a room full of children. Who paid? A department buying ten thousand, so cheap, tough and stackable beat beautiful. What is wrong with it? Tall learners are squashed, the shelf collects rubbish, the frame rusts. Now reverse it: the brief the designer started from. Tough, cheap seating for eleven to fourteen year olds, safe, easy to clean, ten years of use. Do the same with a radio, a phone, a kettle, a taxi door. Every object is an answer. Learn to read the question.
visual_style: Whiteboard desk with labels popping onto each feature, then a brief writing itself in a box beside it; a radio and phone appear with the same label treatment.
mood: Curious and empowering, the ordinary classroom turned into evidence.
pacing: Rapid feature-by-feature labelling, a beat on who pays and what is wrong, then the brief reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the brief behind one object in your kitchen.
